message.content: Lions mate during a brief but intense courtship period that typically lasts only a few days. Male lions will often form coalitions—groups of related males—that compete for access to females. When a female comes into estrus (which occurs roughly once a month), she signals her readiness through vocalizations and scent marking. Males will approach, sniff, and may engage in playful or aggressive displays. Once a male has won the right to mate, he will mount the female and copulate, which can last from a few minutes up to an hour. After mating, the male may guard the female to protect her from rival males. This short mating window is crucial because it allows the male to fertilize multiple females in quick succession, maximizing his reproductive success.
